claims.claim: Customer and government concentration are directly source-addressed execution risks: Infleqtion's Q2 2026 10-Q reports Customer A at 82% of Q2 revenue and 74% of first-half revenue; one customer represented 40% of accounts receivable at June 30, 2026.

The concentration is economically material but not by itself evidence of deterioration: the same filing reports no credit losses since inception, while the risk channel is procurement timing, customer-specific execution and bargaining concentration rather than demonstrated collectability failure.

Reported liquidity should be separated from normalized operating self-funding: Q2 cash flow included a $27.4M temporary payroll-tax working-capital benefit, while management described approximately $14M operating cash burn excluding that timing item.

risks.risk: A single customer represented 82% of Q2 2026 revenue and 74% of first-half revenue, creating customer/procurement concentration sensitivity.
Temporary working-capital timing can overstate near-term cash-generation quality if read without normalization.

contradictions.contradiction: Rapid reported revenue growth coexists with unusually high single-customer concentration; growth therefore does not yet demonstrate broad customer diversification.
contradictions.disposition: observed concentration risk for Alpha underwriting; not a present blocker by itself

unknowns.unknown: Durability of revenue growth after normalizing for Customer A and the degree to which future commercial customers diversify government/customer concentration remain open.
